newsitem.title: USA: Philip Morris, RJR debt widen on tobacco news.
newsitem.headline: Philip Morris, RJR debt widen on tobacco news.

text.p: Philip Morris Cos Inc and RJR Nabisco Holdings Corp debt widened five to ten basis points on Thursday, corporate bond traders said.
News that the nation's state attorney generals are close to a tobacco settlement with Liggett Group Inc, a unit of Brooke Group Ltd caused spreads on tobacco bonds to widen and stocks to drop.
"Tobacco has been the focus today," said one high-grade trader. "Spreads widened between five-to-ten basis points depending on the issue."
RJR Nabisco's 8-3/4 debt due 2007 was offered at 200 basis points over Treasuries, traders said.
"I'd say that's wider by at least 10 to 15 basis points from the beginning of this week," one trader said of RJR's debt.
Philip Morris debt was also seen trading wider by about five basis points, traders added.
As part of the settlement, Ligget Group is expected to hand over potentially damaging documents against the tobacco industry.
Shares of Philip Morris, the nation's largest cigarette company fell $6.25 to $115.875 in early afternoon trading on the New York Stock Exchange, where it was the most heavily traded issue.
RJR Nabisco stock fell 1/2 to 31-3/4; however, Liggett parent, Brooke Group Ltd, added 62.5 cents to $4.875, also on the New York Stock Exchange.
RJR Nabisco's senior debt is currently rated BBB-minus by Standard & Poor's and Baa3 by Moody's Investors Service.
Philip Morris Cos' senior unsecured debt is rated single-A by Standad & Poor's and A2 by Moody's Investors Service.
A news conference is expected later today, to annouce the settlement between Liggett Group and the state attornies general, a source close to the talks told Reuters.
